cards.front: What four properties should evaluation success criteria have?
cards.back: Specific, measurable, achievable and relevant, with a numeric threshold (e.g. F1 >= 0.85 on a held-out set).

cards.front: Two latency measurements to report?
cards.back: Time to first token (TTFT) and total/baseline latency, at percentiles such as p95/p99 rather than averages.

cards.front: Agent eval: transcript vs outcome?
cards.back: Transcript = full record of a trial (outputs, tool calls, reasoning). Outcome = final state of the environment. Grade the outcome, not what the agent claims.

cards.front: pass@k vs pass^k?
cards.back: pass@k: at least one of k trials succeeds (best-of-k use). pass^k: all k trials succeed (production reliability).

cards.front: A safety metric that only counts harmful outputs is missing what?
cards.back: Over-refusal rate on benign requests.

cards.front: Safety vs security metrics?
cards.back: Safety = harmful or off-policy output. Security = resistance to misuse, e.g. prompt-injection success rate, unauthorized tool calls.

cards.front: Grader preference order (fastest to slowest)?
cards.back: Code-based (exact/string match, schema, tests) -> similarity metrics (cosine, ROUGE-L) -> LLM-as-judge with rubric -> human review.

cards.front: Volume or quality for eval sets?
cards.back: Volume: more cases with automated, slightly noisier grading beat a few hand-graded ones.

cards.front: Edge cases every eval set should include?
cards.back: From the docs: irrelevant or nonexistent input, overly long input, poor/harmful/irrelevant user input, and ambiguous cases where humans disagree. Add domain extras: typos/slang, sarcasm, and cases where the right answer is 'I don't know' or a refusal.

cards.front: How many cases to start an eval with?
cards.back: Small: about 20 real queries (research-agent team) or 20-50 tasks from real failures, then grow.

cards.front: Capability vs regression evals?
cards.back: Capability evals target weaknesses (low initial pass rate). Regression evals protect working behavior (near 100% pass) and run on every change.

cards.front: Four ways to make an LLM judge trustworthy?
cards.back: Specific rubric, constrained parseable output, a different model from the one evaluated, calibration against human grades (and repeat runs for consistency).

cards.front: Why is ROUGE a poor factual-accuracy grader?
cards.back: It rewards surface word overlap, not truth or groundedness.

cards.front: Which API suits large eval runs?
cards.back: Message Batches API: 50% cheaper, async, results within 24 hours.

cards.front: Golden rule of A/B testing a prompt?
cards.back: Change one variable at a time; same eval suite, graders and conditions for both variants.

cards.front: Why run multiple trials per case in an A/B test?
cards.back: Outputs are non-deterministic; a small difference may be within run-to-run variance.

cards.front: Offline A/B -> ? -> ? -> full rollout
cards.back: Shadow mode (live traffic, output not shown), then canary/staged rollout, then full online A/B or rollout.

cards.front: Variant B wins accuracy but breaks regression cases. Ship?
cards.back: No. Regressions block shipping; also check cost and latency criteria.

cards.front: Purpose of a held-out set?
cards.back: Detect over-fitting: never tune against it, use it to confirm improvements generalize.

cards.front: Anthropic's tool-improvement loop?
cards.back: Run realistic evals, collect accuracy, runtime, tokens, tool calls and errors; have Claude analyze transcripts and suggest fixes; verify on a held-out set.

cards.front: RAG gives confident wrong answers after a document refresh; model and latency unchanged. Look where first?
cards.back: Retrieval/indexing: stale or irrelevant chunks, incomplete re-index, mismatched embedding model, filters.

cards.front: Signs of a prompt failure?
cards.back: Inconsistent output on similar inputs that improves with explicit criteria, examples or an output format.

cards.front: Five ways to reduce hallucinations?
cards.back: Allow 'I don't know'; extract quotes first; verify with citations; restrict to provided docs; compare best-of-N for consistency.

cards.front: Why use nullable fields in an extraction schema?
cards.back: So the model can return null for absent data instead of inventing a value; retries cannot create missing data.

cards.front: How do you prove model mismatch?
cards.back: Run the same eval set on candidate models; compare quality, latency and cost. Under-powered: fails reasoning-heavy cases. Over-powered: a smaller model passes the threshold.

cards.front: Truncated JSON with stop_reason max_tokens: fix?
cards.back: Raise max_tokens or shorten the requested output. It is a limit problem, not a model problem.

cards.front: When should you start optimizing latency/cost?
cards.back: After the prompt works well without constraints; validate each optimization with evals.

cards.front: Prompt caching: price of write vs read?
cards.back: Write 1.25x base input (5-min TTL) or 2x (1-hour); read 0.1x base input on most models (0.05x on Opus 5.5, 0.025x on Fable 5.1). 5-min cache pays off after 1 read, 1-hour after 2.

cards.front: Prompt caching limits and ordering?
cards.back: Up to 4 breakpoints; default TTL 5 min (refreshed on hit), 1 h optional; prefix order tools -> system -> messages; stable first, volatile last.

cards.front: Caching isn't working. Which usage fields show it?
cards.back: cache_creation_input_tokens and cache_read_input_tokens both 0 (often the prefix is below the model's minimum cacheable length, e.g. 512 tokens on Opus/Sonnet 5.5 but 4,096 on Haiku 4.5, or the prefix changes between calls).

cards.front: Message Batches API trade-off?
cards.back: 50% off input and output; most finish under 1 h but up to 24 h; stacks with caching; not for blocking or user-facing calls.

cards.front: What does streaming improve?
cards.back: Perceived latency (TTFT to the user). Not total generation time or cost.

cards.front: Better way to shorten responses than word counts?
cards.back: Sentence or paragraph limits; LLMs count tokens, not words.

cards.front: Does max_tokens count toward the OTPM rate limit?
cards.back: No. OTPM counts output actually generated.

cards.front: Why segment quality metrics in monitoring?
cards.back: Aggregates hide failing segments (language, product, customer tier).

cards.front: Why include high-confidence outputs in human review samples?
cards.back: Confident errors are missed if only low-confidence or flagged outputs are reviewed.

cards.front: Usage & Cost Admin API endpoints and key?
cards.back: /v1/organizations/usage_report/messages (1m/1h/1d buckets) and /v1/organizations/cost_report (USD, daily only). Requires an Admin API credential (sk-ant-admin... key); workspace API keys are rejected. Data appears within about 5 minutes.

cards.front: Enable Claude Code OpenTelemetry?
cards.back: CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_TELEMETRY=1 plus OTEL exporter settings; prompt text is redacted unless OTEL_LOG_USER_PROMPTS=1.

cards.front: What closes the loop between monitoring and evaluation?
cards.back: Turning production failures into new eval and regression cases.
